changes.oldText: The Dashboard provides an at-a-glance summary of your current resource usage, available limits, and session information across all your projects and resource groups. It helps you quickly understand how your computing resources are being utilized and monitor your recent activities in the system.
changes.oldHtml: The Dashboard provides an at-a-glance summary of your current resource usage, available limits, and session information across all your projects and resource groups. It helps you quickly understand how your computing resources are being utilized and monitor your recent activities in the system.

changes.newText: The Dashboard is the first page you see after logging in. It summarizes your own sessions, resources, folders, deployments, and recent activity in the current project, and holds the actions that used to live on the Start page. Every card counts only what you own in the current project. Cards that depend on a resource group or a time range keep their own setting; see Card Settings.

changes.newText: Get started items: Start Interactive Session, Start Batch Session, Create New Storage Folder, Start Deployment, and Start From URL. Each card runs the same action the Start page offered; see Start Actions for details. A card whose menu is disabled by your administrator is not offered.

changes.oldText: My Total Resource Usage: Displays the resources you are currently using across all your projects. Each resource shows a usage bar below its value; hover over the bar to see how much of your total limit that usage represents. When multiple limits (domain, project, or keypair) apply, the most restrictive one takes effect.

changes.oldText: My Resources in Resource Group: Shows your current resource usage and remaining capacity within the selected resource group of your current project. You can switch groups using the dropdown menu.

changes.oldText: Folder Status: Shows how many storage folders you can reach, split into My Folders, Project Folders, and Invited Folders. When invitations are waiting for you, click the Invited Folders count to open the Data page and review them.

changes.oldText: When you are logged in as a superadmin, the Dashboard page also displays Agent Statistics and Active Agents panels alongside the standard user panels. These panels show cluster-wide agent health and resource utilization. The My Sessions panel is titled Active Sessions for superadmins; it still counts the sessions of the current project.

changes.oldText: Your customized layout is automatically saved and persists across browser sessions. The layout is stored per user, so each user can have their own preferred arrangement. To discard your arrangement and restore the default one, click the Reset layout button at the bottom of the edit sidebar and confirm. Resetting the layout does not remove your custom panels.

changes.newText: Click the Edit button next to the refresh button at the top right of the dashboard to open the edit sidebar beside the board, and Close to hide it again. Its Cards list shows every card you can place on this dashboard, grouped by kind, with a search box above it. Check a card to add it to the board and uncheck it to remove it; you can add it back at any time. A card that cannot be used in this environment is listed but disabled.

changes.oldText: The entire custom-panel feature is hidden until you turn on Custom dashboard panels in the Experimental features section of the User Settings page. If you turn the feature off later, your existing custom panels are hidden — not deleted — and reappear with their saved board positions once you turn it back on.

changes.oldText: Click the Edit button at the top right of the page to open the custom-panel sidebar, and Close to hide it again. The sidebar lists your custom panels. A custom panel shows a data source you select, narrowed by a condition you define. The panel itself shows only a title and its data, so give the panel a title that describes its condition.

changes.oldText: The dashboard refreshes its data automatically every 15 seconds, so the panels always reflect recent activity without reloading the page. Custom panels refresh on the same cycle as the built-in panels.
changes.oldHtml:
The dashboard refreshes its data automatically every 15 seconds, so the panels
always reflect recent activity without reloading the page. Custom panels
refresh on the same cycle as the built-in panels.

changes.newText: The refresh button at the top right of the dashboard is the only refresh control on the page: click it to reload every card at once. The arrow next to it sets how often the dashboard refreshes by itself (off, or every 5 seconds to 10 minutes; 30 seconds by default), and the choice is saved with your board. Cards whose data changes slowly, such as folder counts, refresh less often than the interval you choose.
